events.title: La Llorona - World Film Forum
events.description: La Llorona Jayro Bustamante, 2019, 97 min, Guatemala Presented by Cara Kinnally, Associate Professor of Spanish. An aging former Guatemalan general is tried for his role in the massacre of Indigenous Maya communities during the country’s civil war. Although initially found guilty, the verdict is overturned, and he retreats to his heavily guarded mansion with his wife, daughter, and granddaughter. As protesters gather outside to denounce his crimes, a series of unsettling and unexplained events begins inside the home following the arrival of Alma, a mysterious new domestic worker. Drawing on the Guatemalan legend of La Llorona, the ghost of a woman condemned to wander in search of her lost children, director Jayro Bustamante reimagines the familiar tale as a powerful exploration of historical memory, state repression, gender violence, and the pursuit of justice.

events.title: 2026 SUPPLY CHAIN CONSULTING LECTURE SERIES
events.description: PURDUE STUDENTS ARE INVITED Students across Purdue majors and programs are warmly invited to attend any or all sessions. Join us to learn directly from industry professionals, ask questions, explore career paths, and connect classroom ideas with real-world supply chain and consulting practice. ABOUT THE SERIES The 2026 Supply Chain Consulting Lecture Series connects Purdue students with experienced supply chain executives, consultants, alumni, and industry professionals to explore how organizations solve complex supply chain and operations challenges in practice. The series is an integral part of SCOM 469 — Supply Chain and Operations Analytics Consulting, a 3-credit experiential learning course that transforms the classroom into a professional consulting environment. Student teams apply supply chain theory, data analytics, AI-enabled tools, and structured consulting methods to real-world business and industry challenges. THE THREE-PILLAR EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING MODEL Consulting & Industry Study Projects — Students learn by solving real business and industry problems through corporate-sponsored consulting engagements and advisor-guided industry studies.Mentoring Program — Experienced alumni and industry professionals coach student teams on problem solving, analytics, project management, executive storytelling, and professional development. Jeffrey R. Powers, retired IBM executive and Purdue alumnus, chairs the Industry Advisory Board.Industry Lecture Series — Practitioners bring current challenges, emerging technologies, leadership lessons, and real-world decision making directly into the classroom. SCOM 469 builds on Purdue’s university–industry partnerships and experiential projects with organizations including Wabash, Rolls-Royce, Corteva, Taste, and other corporate and industry partners. For Fall 2026, students will work through two experiential project pathways: the corporate project Taste Omnichannel Dining Service Optimization and the industry study Enhancing Pharmaceutical Supply-Chain Resilience. WHY ATTEND? Learn from experienced professionals — See how practitioners approach ambiguous, high-impact supply chain problems.Understand professional practice — Explore consulting, leadership, sourcing, planning, program management, and digital transformation in action.Connect analytics and AI to execution — See how data, analytics, and AI shape consulting strategy and day-to-day supply chain decisions.Connect classroom frameworks to real decisions — Examine constraints, cross-functional trade-offs, and the realities of implementation.Build your professional network — Meet Purdue alumni and experienced industry professionals while exploring supply chain career paths.All Purdue students are welcome. You do not need to be enrolled in SCOM 469 to participate. Attend the sessions that match your interests, come prepared to ask questions and share perspectives, and use the series as an opportunity to learn and build professional connections. FALL 2026 LECTURE SCHEDULE SEPTEMBER 3 — Consulting 101 Isaac Tipton — CEO, Prowire USA The opening session introduces the foundations of consulting and structured problem solving. Drawing on professional experience, the speakers will discuss how consultants approach ambiguous business problems, work with clients and teams, communicate insights, and translate analysis into actionable recommendations. SEPTEMBER 17 — Program Management in Supply Chain: From Plan to Execution Michelle Kozlowski — Senior Program Manager, Amazon Catherine “Cathy” Nash — Sales & Operations Execution Planner, Constellation Brands Strong strategies create value only when organizations can execute them. This session focuses on program management, planning, coordination, accountability, and execution—examining how supply chain professionals move from plans and priorities to operational results across people, processes, and functions. OCTOBER 1 — Trade-Off Management + Cross-Functional Procurement & Sourcing Decisions Amanda Tronchin — Finance & Strategy Consultant, Pinnacle Strategy Group Eduardo Da Silva-Witzke — Aftermarket Sourcing Analyst, Cummins Inc. Supply chain and procurement decisions frequently require balancing competing objectives across cost, service, risk, quality, capacity, and strategic priorities. This session explores how professionals structure trade-offs, collaborate across functions, and translate financial, operational, and strategic considerations into sourcing and procurement decisions. OCTOBER 15 — Leadership, Influence & the Human Side of Supply Chain Consulting Kriti Gupta — Director of Operations, Amazon Nilo Cedeno-Guadamud — Global Category Manager, Wabash Analytics alone rarely produces organizational change. This session explores the human side of supply chain leadership and consulting—including stakeholder influence, relationship building, communication, team leadership, negotiation, and the ability to move organizations from insight to action. OCTOBER 29 — AI in Supply Chain: From Consulting Strategy to Everyday Execution Vishal Madisetti — Associate, Emerging Platforms, KPMG US Brookelle Mathieson — Life Sciences Supply Chain Management Consultant, Accenture Possible contributor: Khushi Karmokar — Procurement Analyst, ThoughtSpot AI is changing both how consultants solve problems and how supply chain professionals perform everyday work. This session explores practical applications of AI, analytics, automation, and emerging technologies—from consulting strategy and transformation initiatives to operational decision support, procurement, and day-to-day execution. NOVEMBER 12 — Planning, Constraints & Supply Chain Systems Thinking Kyle Harshbarger — Supply Chain Engineer, Marathon Petroleum Lauren Heiss — Senior Technology Consultant, EY The final session brings together planning, constraints, technology, and systems thinking. The speakers will connect MRP/ERP concepts, bottlenecks, lessons from The Goal, and real-world planning challenges to the broader question of how supply chains operate as interconnected systems. The session will also explore supply chain career paths and how the strategic role of the supply chain function varies across industries. CONNECTING INDUSTRY AND THE CLASSROOM The Industry Lecture Series is not designed as a collection of stand-alone guest presentations. Each session is integrated with students’ consulting and industry-study work. Student teams are encouraged to bring questions from their projects into the classroom, apply lessons from speakers to their analyses, and reflect on how different professionals approach similar challenges across industries. Student ambassadors will also work directly with speakers before selected sessions to help prepare and contextualize the lectures, providing another opportunity to develop professional communication, stakeholder-management, and networking skills. events.title: Executive Forum with Vivek Chakrabortty, Chief Executive Officer for The Kavi Group LLC
events.description: The Executive Forum is open to the public, as seating permits, and provides opportunities for the exchange of ideas and discussion of topics and issues facing business and management. Vivek was born in Mumbai, India, in a Brahmin Hindu and Catholic household and grew up in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, a Muslim country. One grandfather was an Indian Freedom Fighter, and the other was in the British Navy. From a very young age, my parents instilled an empathetic, diverse way of thinking in Vivek and his brother. His love for travel and desire to know people with different backgrounds and life stories is rooted in his own diversity. You could say he has been a risk taker and entrepreneur his whole life. He grew up in the rigorous and structured CBSE Indian school system where you had to choose between science, commerce, or arts at the age of 16. He craved freedom and knew that a path in America would enable him to be whomever he wanted to be. He negotiated with his dad to attend high school and college in the US, and moved when he was just 16. His life forever changed. It was only by chance that he started to work in operations resilience before two major US events happened: 9/11 and Hurricane Katrina. As a business continuity and crisis management consultant, he learned that businesses must be one step ahead of the threats faced by their clients whether they are natural disasters, civic unrest, terrorism, active shooters, cyber-security breaches, technology failures, or catastrophic accidents. He was the emergency preparedness advisor to the Louisiana Recovery Authority in the aftermath of hurricanes Katrina and Rita and led the California Healthcare Surge Planning which was the first of its kind in the U.S. in terms of scale and scope. The teams he led on these two projects were awarded the Chairman’s Award, PwC’s highest recognition for outstanding client service. In the past 25 years, he has worked in the American South, Northeast, Midwest, Pacific Northwest, California, and Mid-Atlantic. His work has taken him to Europe, Australia, and Asia. These experiences as well as his understanding of culture and people prepared him to be an entrepreneur. In 2014, his wife Kathy and Vivek invested their life savings to start the Kavi Group, a management consulting firm that provides business continuity and crisis management advisory services. Today, Kavi Group is a 7-figure company with Fortune 100 companies as their clients. Kavi has helped our clients navigate the COVID19 pandemic, supply chain risks and disruptions, geo-political conflicts, climate-change associated threats, and adjust to the new normal of risk management.
